wu: Travel Pictionary: Students draw a travel-related word (e.g., 'beach', 'hotel', 'passport') on the board while others guess. The drawer says 'It's a place you go to...' or 'It's something you use for...' to elicit vocabulary.
wuAlt: Travel Charades: Students act out travel verbs (e.g., 'check-in', 'board a plane') while others guess the action.
Word Association: Teacher says 'travel', students take turns saying related words (e.g., 'suitcase', 'flight', 'destination').
pres: Show flashcards of famous Moroccan cities (Marrakech, Casablanca, Chefchaouen). Model sentences: 'Marrakech is the most exciting city I have ever visited.' 'Chefchaouen has the bluest streets.' Check understanding by asking 'Which city is the most...?' and having students complete sentences.
presAlt: Travel Story: Read a short story about a trip to Morocco using superlatives (e.g., 'The best meal I had was in Fez.').', 'Realia: Bring in photos of travel souvenirs (e.g., a tagine, a carpet) and have students compare them using superlatives.
prac: Superlative Sort: Students work in pairs to match superlative adjectives (e.g., 'biggest', 'most beautiful') to pictures of landmarks (e.g., Hassan II Mosque, Atlas Mountains). Teacher monitors and corrects errors.
pracAlt: Find Someone Who...: Students walk around asking 'Have you ever been to the most... place in Morocco?' and fill in a grid.
Superlative Race: In teams, students race to write superlative sentences about famous places in Morocco.
ls: Listen to a short podcast about travel experiences. Students fill in gaps in sentences like 'The best thing about the trip was ________.' and 'The most difficult part was ________.'
re: Travel Relay: Students line up and take turns running to the board to write a superlative sentence about a travel topic (e.g., 'The best food in Morocco is ________.').
prod: Best-of City Presentations: In triads, students prepare a 2-minute presentation about the best place they have ever visited. They must use present perfect and superlatives (e.g., 'I have been to Agadir, and it has the most beautiful beaches.').
rw: Read a short review of a Moroccan hotel. Students underline all superlatives and then write their own 50-word review of a hotel or restaurant using at least three superlatives.
st: Watch a 2-minute video clip of a travel vlogger in Morocco. Close with the goodbye routine: 'Today we learned to describe trips using superlatives. Thank you for your participation.'
g: Students create bingo cards with superlative adjectives and mark them off when the teacher calls them out.
Students describe a travel word using superlatives without saying the word itself.
Students describe a place using superlatives (e.g., 'It's the oldest medina in Morocco.') for others to guess.
Students sit in a circle and take turns adding a superlative to a sentence (e.g., 'I have visited the most... place, which is...').
Teams race to draw and guess travel words using superlatives.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 100-word paragraph about the best trip they have ever taken.
Support: Use a sentence frame: 'The best ________ I have ever seen is ________ because ________.'
hw: Write a 80-word email to a friend describing the best place you have ever visited using superlatives.
Record a 1-minute voice message about your best travel experience using superlatives.
Read a travel review online and write down 5 superlatives used.
tip: Encourage students to share personal travel experiences from Morocco or abroad to make the language practice more meaningful and relevant to their lives.
